title: Building a Small Function Library
subtopics: Refactoring Script Code into Reusable Functions
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of building a small function library and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply organizing related functions in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Building a Small Function Library is part of Functions and Reusable Programming. Start with organizing related functions and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: Functions make behavior reusable; clear arguments, scope and return values make that behavior testable.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Functions make behavior reusable; clear arguments, scope and return values make that behavior testable. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Call the function with typical, empty and invalid inputs, and inspect what it returns. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Building a Small Function Library
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 73: Building a Small Function Library
add_offset <- function(x, offset = 5) x + offset
add_offset(3)

content_blocks.limitations: Make inputs and return values explicit; also test an empty or invalid argument. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For building a small function library, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
